messages:
anya: CI perf alert: small-sequence end-to-end latency up ~1.6x after last nightly image (torch 2.5.1, triton 2.7.0). stack: inference/runtime smallbatch bench. Rolling CI graph attached in build.
sam: ack. which benchmark exactly? smallseq = batch=1, seq=64, fp16 KV cache warm?
anya: yes. repro locally on a100-hosted image: baseline (torch2.5.0/triton2.6) 45ms p50, new image ~72ms p50. p95 also worse. reproducible on dev machine.
nisha: can you paste quick perf output? also any kernel names hot?
anya: pasted short perf snippet:
```
Top kernels by time:
- matmul_opt_dispatch_bin_128x128_fp16: 40%
- fallback_gemm_smallbatch_fp16: 33%   <-- up from 5% baseline
- softmax_attn_kernel: 12%
- kv_prefetch_worker: 8% (more wakeups)
```

sam: hmm fallback_gemm_smallbatch... that sounds like autotune or selector flipped to fallback kernel. Could be triton autotune table invalidation after nvrtc change.
jake: also seeing increased CPU wakeups from kv_prefetch; maybe prefetch thread backoff heuristic changed in runtime combined with slightly slower matmul -> more concurrency.
anya: I ruled out scheduler/cgroups differences (same container flags). I can repro with pinned driver 12.6 and both images; only image diff matters.
ryan: any errors in triton logs about autotune misses or kernel cache misses?
anya: triton logs show lines like:
```
[autotune] candidate list empty for op id 0x7f2a, falling back to generic_gemm
[cuda] nvrtc: compiled kernel sha mismatch, cleared autotune cache
```

nisha: that nvrtc line is suspicious. Could be a change in nvrtc version in the image that affects kernel hash. If autotune table gets invalidated, autotune will pick a safe but slower kernel until it rebuilds—explains spike.
sam: we need to know if autotune rebuilds during CI windows or if fallback persists. Can you check if successive runs improve (i.e., autotune warms up)?
anya: ran 5 sequential runs: iteration1 72ms, iter2 69ms, iter3 68ms, iter4 67ms, iter5 66ms — some warmup but still ~45ms baseline not recovered. autotune rebuild not fully restoring perf.
ryan: maybe kernel selectors changed and the new compiled kernels are different codepaths (tiling/strides) leading to higher latency for small-seq shapes. Could be a kernel codegen change in triton/torch.
jake: plan: bisect image layers to find which package bump caused it (torch, triton, nvrtc, cuda-toolkit). We should test images with combos.
sam: also create a minimal reproducer: single small model run with --triton-autotune=off and with cache dir persistent to observe selection. We can try forcing old kernel via env to confirm.
anya: reproducer command I used:
```
python bench_infer.py --model tiny-transformer --batch 1 --seq 64 --dtype fp16 --warmup 20 --iters 100
CONTAINER_IMAGE=redwood/runtime-nightly:torch2.5.1-triton2.7
```

nisha: I can run a quick smoke across image variants on CI matrix (torch 2.5.0|2.5.1 x triton 2.6|2.7 x nvrtc v11|v12). spinning up now, will post results.
infra-bot: perf-ci: job 14231 queued (matrix size 8) — link: https://ci.redwood.ai/14231
sam: if bisect points to nvrtc/triton change, we should hold rollout of the nightly image and pin dedicated`s canary to previous image. Also open a revert PR for the offending package bump if it's a single linear change.
anya: quick local test: launching with TRITON_DISABLE_AUTOTUNE=1 returns p50 ~50ms (closer), so autotune path likely the issue (fallback vs tuned kernel choice). disabling autotune is not acceptable for prod but useful for root cause.
ryan: good signal. Can you capture cuobjdump names for compiled kernels in both images? kernel SASS shows tiling differences.
anya: attached trimmed cuobjdump diff (paste):
```
# baseline kernel name: matmul_opt_tile8x128_fp16
# new kernel name: matmul_generic_tile16x64_fp16
# instruction mix: new kernel has more shared-loads and larger register spill
```

jake: that matches selector choosing a different strategy. Next steps: Nisha's matrix results -> if triton bump is root cause, reproduce minimal repro and file bug with triton autotune table invalidation + nvrtc hash churn.
sam: also add a short-term mitigation: pin triton version for nightly and patch deploy pipeline to avoid promoting image until fixed. I'll open a PR to pin to triton 2.6 in the image build.
anya: noted. I'll keep hold on the canary rollout and add the reproducer and logs to the incident thread.
nisha: matrix done: failures correlate 2.7 triton + nvrtc v12 variant. torch bump alone didn't trigger. So triage points to triton 2.7 + nvrtc12 compile hash behavior.
ryan: OK. open issue with triton/ops we depend on and attach cuobjdump+perf. Also ask triton team if there is a known autotune cache schema change between 2.6->2.7.
sam: I'll draft a rollback image and pin for canary. Anya, Nisha — please keep updating. If we confirm single-package root cause we do a hotfix revert.
anya: will do. adding checklist: reproduce minimal, bisect exact triton commit if possible, file triton issue, pin image, hold canary. Also notify product/ops about potential impact.
ryan: thanks. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: perf-ci: job 14231 completed — 3 failures, 5 passed. link: https://ci.redwood.ai/14231
